questions.claim: The Atlantic hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November. Think of an average season, judged by 1991 to 2020. An average season has more than 4 named storms.
questions.fact: NOAA's National Hurricane Center: an average Atlantic season (1991 to 2020) has 14 named storms, 7 hurricanes and 3 major hurricanes.
questions.why: Seasons vary a lot, but the long-run average is a good anchor: about half of the named storms become hurricanes, and a bit under half of the hurricanes become major ones.

questions.lead: A scheduled domestic flight by one of the big US airlines is due to take off in 2024.
questions.ask: More than 40% of flights like it arrive on time (less than 15 minutes late).
questions.claim: A scheduled domestic flight by one of the big US airlines is due to take off in 2024. More than 40% of flights like it arrive on time (less than 15 minutes late).
questions.fact: BTS: in 2024 the big US airlines posted an on-time arrival rate of 78.10%, down from 78.34% in 2023. (On time means less than 15 minutes late.)
questions.why: Most flights land on time, but about one in five does not: delays are common enough that you should plan for them.

questions.lead: A US recession has just ended and the next one is some way off. Think of the expansions between recessions since 1945.
questions.ask: On average, an expansion lasted more than 240 months.
questions.claim: A US recession has just ended and the next one is some way off. Think of the expansions between recessions since 1945. On average, an expansion lasted more than 240 months.
questions.fact: NBER's business cycle dates: since 1945 the average US expansion lasted 64.2 months, a little over five years.
questions.why: Expansions last years, not months, so a recession is not 'due' just because the last one was a while ago.

questions.lead: A member of the US Congress runs for re-election in the general election of 2022 or 2024.
questions.ask: More than 95% of incumbents like them win.
questions.claim: A member of the US Congress runs for re-election in the general election of 2022 or 2024. More than 95% of incumbents like them win.
questions.fact: Ballotpedia: congressional incumbents who ran for another term won at a 98% rate in the general elections of both 2024 and 2022.
questions.why: Incumbency is a big advantage: nearly every sitting member of Congress who runs wins again. When a question is about the usual outcome, start there, then look for what is unusual this time.

questions.lead: A psychology study published in 2008 reported a statistically significant result. A team of over 270 researchers re-runs 100 studies like it, following the original methods.
questions.ask: More than 50% of the re-runs also find a significant result.
questions.claim: A psychology study published in 2008 reported a statistically significant result. A team of over 270 researchers re-runs 100 studies like it, following the original methods. More than 50% of the re-runs also find a significant result.
questions.fact: In the Open Science Collaboration's 2015 project, 97% of the original studies had reported a significant result but only 36% of the 100 re-runs did.
questions.why: A published, significant result is a weaker signal than it looks: when 100 studies were re-run, far fewer than the originals' near-universal success held up.
questions.src_name: Open Science Collaboration (Science, 2015), reported by the Association for Psychological Science
